plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Huge, lush, often fragrant blooms open from fat round buds, with layered petals that look like silk ruffles. Plants form lush mounds of glossy, deeply cut green leaves that set off the flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (roughly May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Gardens across temperate North America and Europe, native to China, Mongolia and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and flower for decades, sometimes more than 50 years, in the same spot. Ants often crawl over the buds, drawn to the sweet nectar they secrete.

plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: A tough, thorny shrub with crinkled, deep green leaves and wide, open, fragrant flowers. In late summer and autumn, plump, tomato-red hips follow the blooms. It thrives on windswept dunes and coastal paths.
plants.bloomingSeason: June through late summer, with sporadic repeat blooms into autumn
plants.location: Coastal dunes and gardens of the temperate Northern Hemisphere, native to East Asia
plants.funFact: The vitamin C-rich hips of this rose have been used to make jams, teas and syrups. The shrub's salt tolerance makes it a natural dune stabilizer.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia
plants.description: A gnarled coastal tree crowned with upright, candle-like flower spikes. Each spike is made of hundreds of tiny, tightly packed blooms, and they glow against silvery-backed leaves. Honeyeaters and lorikeets flock to them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn and winter in the Southern Hemisphere, including June
plants.location: Eastern coast of Australia, from Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria
plants.funFact: After flowering, the spikes become woody cones that hold seeds. Many Banksias release those seeds in response to fire, so the plant is well adapted to regenerating after bushfires.
